chain_focus: Google TPU v8t (training) generation — the training-optimized v8 SKU with high HBM4 capacity and heavy optical/OCS scale-up interconnect. Host CPU migrates from x86 to custom Arm Axion 2. From fab tools and HBM4 through TSMC fabrication, Broadcom co-design and CoWoS packaging to OCS-interconnected training pods serving Google DeepMind (Gemini training) and Anthropic. Generation- and workload-separated from TPU v7 (Ironwood) and the inference SKU TPU v8i.

players.product: Gemini frontier-model training on TPU v8t
Claude model training on TPU v8t
TPU v8t training pods (OCS-interconnected) in Google Cloud

quarterly_data.signal: At Cloud Next, Google introduced its 8th-generation TPUs, individually specialized for training vs serving. TPU 8t (training) provides ~3x the processing of Ironwood (TPU v7) and 2x the performance, built for the most demanding agentic training workloads.

players.product: TPU v8t training-pod system boards & racks

quarterly_data.signal: Strengthening 2027 outlook from two next-generation hyperscaler AI/ML compute programs ramping in 2027 plus a 'digital native' fully-integrated compute+networking rack-scale program entering production in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: next-gen compute programs + digital-native rack ramping 2027

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 enterprise growth to be driven by the ramp of MULTIPLE next-generation AI/ML compute programs (ramps in the half of 2027); AI/ML compute demand 'significantly increased' vs 90 days ago for 2026 and into 2027. Capacity is in place for 2027 demand — the constraint is material (some component lead times well above 52 weeks); customers placed non-cancellable, non-refundable orders for long-lead silicon.
quarterly_data.figure: multiple next-gen AI/ML compute programs ramping 2027; demand > guided revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation compute (management): Celestica has 'already won the next generation of that program' (the hyperscaler AI/ML compute program ramping through 2026) and expects those programs 'to actually ramp into 2027'. Looking towards 2027, management anticipates strong demand from hyperscaler and digital native customers driven by ramps in next-gen AI/ML compute programs; on the compute side Celestica focuses on HPS and JDM design-oriented work and has 'several projects in the pipeline to improve those engagements on the HPS side'.
quarterly_data.figure: next-generation program already won; ramp into 2027

players.product: Neoverse CPU IP for Axion 2 host CPU

connects_to.relationship: Arm CPU IP for Axion host (replaces x86)

contracts.signal: TPU v8 (8t/8i) host CPU migrates from x86 to custom Arm Axion 2; per Arm, the largest accelerators (TPU, Trainium, Rubin) are increasingly going 100% Arm

Google stated that its Arm-based Axion CPU is a CORE COMPONENT of its AI infrastructure strategy and THE HOST CPU for its latest TPU AI systems. Arm called out 'strong deployments from partners like Google with their Axion, with all the new TPU deployments' as a driver of cloud-AI royalty overperformance, and cited Axion as proof Arm coexists with proprietary accelerators — Google 'used Axion as an interface into their TPUs, away from x86'.

quarterly_data.signal: Axion confirmed as the host CPU for Google's latest TPU AI systems and a core component of its AI infrastructure strategy. Backdrop: Arm data-center royalty more than doubled YoY again, Neoverse shipments passed 1.5 billion cores (last 500 million in nine months), and IDC reported spending on Arm-based accelerated server platforms has nearly doubled in two quarters and now surpasses x86.
quarterly_data.figure: Axion = host CPU for latest TPU systems; Neoverse >1.5B cores

connects_to.relationship: custom XPU-attach silicon for the TPU ecosystem (AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory interface controllers, near-memory compute) under an expanded commercial agreement with warrant

quarterly_data.signal: OCS addressable market held at MORE THAN $4 BILLION (doubled from $2B at OFC 2026, 2030 timeframe) and management suggests even that may be conservative — applications have widened from the original scale-out focus to scale-across and now a clear path to SCALE-UP, where there are active customer engagements. OCS revenue grew sequentially in Q4 and is expected to grow significantly through fiscal 2027 as production expands across two manufacturing locations, spanning the 320x320 platform and other system sizes. 1.6T transceivers are ramping rapidly through calendar 2026 into 2027, with the ramp pulled in versus the prior quarter's assumptions.
quarterly_data.figure: OCS TAM >$4B and widening to scale-up; OCS revenue growing across two plants; 1.6T ramp pulled in

connects_to.relationship: OCS for TPU pod scale-up interconnect

contracts.signal: MEMS OCS for TPU training-pod scale-up interconnect; Lumentum OCS backlog >$400M and scaling; participant in the OCP OCS project alongside Google, NVIDIA, Coherent, Microsoft

quarterly_data.signal: Per Goldman Sachs, Google's TPU pods use MEMS-based optical circuit switch (OCS) for scale-up interconnect (TPU v7 SuperPod interconnects 9,216 chips via OCS); Lumentum OCS backlog exceeded $400M (Feb 2026) and is scaling rapidly

OCS shipments doubled from fiscal Q3 to fiscal Q4 2026, and Q1 FY2027 guidance includes Lumentum's first triple-digit OCS revenue quarter, expected 'meaningfully above the three-digit mark' ($100M+). Internal manufacturing expansion is progressing smoothly after earlier supply-chain constraints; initial work has started to add capacity with contract manufacturers alongside increased internal factory output. Lumentum is tracking to - not ahead of - its previously stated $400 million of OCS shipments for the second half of calendar 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: OCS shipments 2x QoQ; first $100M+ OCS quarter guided for Q1 FY2027; $400M H2 CY2026 on track

quarterly_data.signal: OCS competitive position: 'we are really the only merchant supplier today of OCS.' Relative to one OCS customer that has an internal source of supply, Michael Hurlston expects that customer will keep using an internal version but that Lumentum 'will absorb the vast majority' of the volume as OCS shipments scale, crossing over to become the number one supplier sometime in early 2027. Demand signal for 2027 'continues to be incredibly strong.'
quarterly_data.figure: only merchant OCS supplier; expects to become #1 OCS supplier early 2027

quarterly_data.signal: OCS roadmap has come into better view since the prior call: Lumentum is now planning higher and lower port count products, including specialized in-tray offerings. These are entirely additive to the OCS TAM presented at OFC, expected to hit in the 2028 timeframe, and require significant engineering redesign.
quarterly_data.figure: higher/lower port-count and in-tray OCS products; additive TAM; 2028 timeframe

quarterly_data.signal: OCS ahead of plan (CEO Michael Hurlston): the OCS business is 'exceeding internal expectations' - Lumentum had targeted its first $10 million OCS quarter for fiscal Q3 and 'cleared that bar three months ahead of schedule.' OCS order backlog 'now has surged well past $400 million, the majority of which is slated for shipment in the second half of this calendar year' (repeated in Q&A as 'primarily deliverable in the back half of the year', although one Q&A answer said 'most of which is going to be shipped in 2027'). The backlog comes from three customers ('It's three customers making up that backlog'), each increasing demand, and deliveries to all three were accelerated this quarter. The calendar Q4 OCS exit previously pegged at around $100 million 'looks like it'll be quite a bit higher than that'; the 2027 run rate is expected to step up again. Lumentum did not split the $400 million between the two quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: first $10 million OCS quarter reached three months early; OCS backlog well past $400 million (three customers); calendar Q4 exit above the prior around $100 million view

quarterly_data.signal: OCS applications (Wupen Yuen, President, Global Business Units): no change to the four dominant OCS use cases - spine replacement, scale-across applications, optical scale-up, and protection/redundancy in the network. All OCS customers use these applications to different degrees; other scenarios may emerge and are being watched, but 'these four, to us today, they're the dominant application scenarios.'
quarterly_data.figure: four dominant OCS applications: spine replacement, scale-across, optical scale-up, protection/redundancy
